opportunities.title: Small grants

amount.raw: Awards generally fall in a range of £1,500-£5,000 and will only exceptionally exceed £6,000. Travel and subsistence up to £2,000 per person for trips up to 13 days or £2,500 per person for 14 days or more; up to £5,000 for PhD fieldwork visits of six months or more. Japan office considers awards up to ¥300,000 for PhD students from Japan.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Applicants must belong to, or provide evidence of support from, an organisation or institution willing to receive grant funds. Applications not accepted from individuals seeking support for personal projects, though the UK office may consider individuals with proof of organisational support. Grant payments cannot be made to personal bank accounts. Previous recipients welcome. No grants for undergraduate or master's students, or for student fees.
opportunities.summary: Seed funding awards to enable UK-Japan projects that might otherwise not be possible. Projects should bring people in the UK and Japan together to deepen mutual understanding, encourage exchange of ideas or expertise, or develop lasting collaboration. Supports festivals, workshops, performances, exchanges, collaborative projects, Japanese language teaching, and academic research/visits/exchange.

opportunities.title: Butterfield Awards in Medicine and Health

amount.raw: Up to £10,000 per award; continuing projects lasting up to three years to a maximum of £10,000 per year, to a total limit of £30,000.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Applicants should normally show an existing research record, but consideration is also given to practitioners, managers, carers or others in health-related fields. Project must involve partners in both the UK and Japan, supported by reputable referees not based at the same institution as either project partner. Preference to those not previously involved in UK-Japan collaboration and early-career applicants. Apply to the UK office regardless of where based.
opportunities.summary: Annual awards supporting exchanges and collaborations between health and medical professionals in Japan and the UK. Broad in application, supporting study of scientific, clinical, social and economic issues in healthcare. Grants may be used for travel expenses, or to contribute to other costs including conference and publication costs.
